packs.title: Canals, Curves and Current
packs.promise: Find three different kinds of Munich space beyond the old town.

q.s: Collect three kinds of line along a garden’s water axis.
st: From a comfortable stopped view, find one straight water edge, one line of planting and one line in the sky or a reflection. If there is no reflection, use the sky.
Describe each line as continuous, broken or curved. Make your own small collection of three words or marks without gathering anything from the park.
Save the three lines and choose the one that most strongly draws your eye along the canal.

q.s: Follow the difference between a roof’s edge and its supports.
st: From a lawful open path or the operator’s photograph, find one dipping roof edge, one tall support and one visible cable line.
Compare the roof’s curved outline with the support’s straighter direction. Trace both with your eyes while staying still.
Save the three observations and a sentence explaining where the roof seems lightest. Do not approach barriers to improve the view.

q.s: Make a short original sequence from an old power station’s silhouette.
st: Look for the tall ochre chimney, a lower roof and the line where planting meets the buildings. Choose three forms that are visible, or use the operator’s photograph.
Write three original scene directions: one that rises, one that settles and one that opens outward. Let the building shapes guide the sequence rather than inventing historical events.
Save your three-beat sequence with a small title of your own. No performance, music recording, event attendance or drawing skill is required.

packs.title: Small Wonders, Wide Skies
packs.promise: Find small surprises between Munich’s busy squares and open garden paths.

q.s: Give the town hall a three-detail introduction.
st: Choose a comfortable, lawful public viewpoint at Marienplatz public square facing Neues Rathaus. Keep the route through the space clear.
Find one pointed shape, one repeated opening, and one carved detail on the New Town Hall facade. Stay clear of the building entrance and moving crowds.
Choose which of the three would still be recognizable in a tiny drawing. Describe the shape without needing to identify a historical figure.
Save the three observations and your tiny-drawing choice.

q.s: Write three frames for a story made of buildings.
st: Choose a comfortable, lawful public viewpoint at Alter Hof public courtyard, enter through the Burgstraße gate if open. Keep the route through the space clear.
Find a passage, a roofline, and a change of material. You can use one viewpoint; no doorway or museum entry is needed.
Imagine an arrival, a pause, and a departure. Write three scene directions using the architecture.
Save the three-frame storyboard as text or a tiny sketch with an optional courtyard photo.

q.s: Make a short garden passage feel like a change of tempo.
st: Choose a comfortable, lawful public viewpoint at Hofgarten western public arcade and adjacent garden path near Odeonsplatz. Keep the route through the space clear.
Choose a comfortable short section of open arcade or parallel garden path. Walk or roll without a speed target, stopping only where you leave room for others.
Notice a repeated opening, a patch of shade, and one change in your view toward the garden. Let those three details mark the passage.
Save three observations in sequence, as a note or optional view photo.
